# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 70 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 48 | Coptic

---

## Saying 70

Jesus said: "If you bring forth what is within you, what you bring forth will save you. If you do not bring forth what is within you, what you do not bring forth will kill you."

---

**Council Notes:**

- "Bring forth" is the standard rendering of the Coptic action verb here; PNEUMA's "give birth to" is a vivid metaphorical expansion that is not linguistically required.
- "Kill you" (EMET) over "destroy you" (LOGOS): the Coptic uses the straightforward death verb (*mou*), not a destruction metaphor.
- The symmetry of the structure is the theological point: the same inner reality is savior or killer depending on whether it is expressed or suppressed.
- This saying has been cited as a parallel to Jung's concept of the shadow, though the Thomasine context is specifically about spiritual self-realization.
